title.narrative: FORSA II

description.narrative: Mercy Corps proposes “Fostering Resilience by Strengthening Abilities II”, a 6.5 million EUR gender responsive programme designed to increase access to education and employment for vulnerable youth from host and refugee communities over the next 3.5 years in two areas of Lebanon: Bekaa and South. Building on its successful training and job placement experience in Lebanon and on its extensive network of stakeholders, Mercy Corps will partner with private and public Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institutes, private companies, local associations, incubators and online and offline job platforms to enable the participation of youth in targeted skillsdevelopment aligning with market needs, to support access of young men and women to self-employment, and to improve job placement mechanisms in Lebanon in a sustainable manner, allowing vulnerable individuals to benefit from improved services beyond the duration of the programme.To strengthen market based TVET provision to address the mismatch of skills to employment, and to strengthen platforms linking job-seekers with employment.

title.narrative: Output 2.2 Percentage of digital skills graduates who register for and graduate from the freelance academy
Output 2.2.1. Number of program participants who graduate from the Freelance academy

description.narrative: In Y2, MC launched the Freelance Academy and estimate that 70 participants should have graduated by the end of Y2. In Y3, MC will further scale up activities and other participants, with the goal of reaching the full target of 170 graduates by the end of Y3. Overall, the target for this activity has been increased from 113 to 280 participants as it has proven very successful in supporting youth accessing freelance jobs, as evident by the high employment rate of this component and the unique opportunity it gives to youth to access much needed hard currency without leaving the country.
